cases.scope: CI-only Windows2022 patched GLib/GIO; registry versus nochange, 0-16 epochs
cases.observed: Original #45015173260 private +221184B, optional REGION +155648B, heap BUSY -7794B; three independent GIO16 runs corroborated signs, not owners. Synthetic Windows2022 calibration #45040046000: controlled test HeapAlloc64/HeapFree48, 16 expected outstanding; ETW started before workload, sequential capture, logger zero-loss checked, xperf totals+size360 stack action PASS. This is NOT a recorded actual exact-16 xperf table count nor any real GIO owner. NEW 2026-11-23 synthetic ETW source-calibration Windows #45044677361 independently matched unique noinline source stack: 64 HeapAlloc(360) calls, 48 frees, 16 intentionally retained (=5,760 requested bytes); zero reported event/log buffer loss. Process-wide 360B size-filter saw ~78-85 total allocations, 16 outstanding; global Alloc KB/count semantics not identical. Proof is ONLY synthetic and NOT GIO leak attribution. 2026-11-23 actual disposable MSVC GIO runtime #45046446784: nochange watch registrations=6, APC completions=0, final pending=6/peak=6; registry 16cycles registrations=23, APC completions=17, final pending=6/peak=6; GIO SDK exports=2047 matched. This is direct *registry watch subscription* bounded-lifetime evidence, NOT overall GIO PrivateUsage leak classification. 2026-11-23 isolated Windows Xperf 16-cycle preworkload CI #45051751198: nochange new HeapAlloc 32101/outstanding0 (stack coverage100%). #45052226913: nochange new HeapAlloc32095/outstanding0; registry 16 cycles completed but HeapSession disappeared at precleanup even with 512MB sequential limit, so REGISTRY owner unknown. Source-guarded last4-of16 CI #45052837535: nochange HeapAlloc8050/out0, complete stack count coverage; registry 4-cycle late capture and loss check/Xperf stack report generation succeeded but original source-stack table parser rejected. Zero nochange outstanding only for events within window, NOT process-wide all alloc/VirtualAlloc or an actual leak-zero proof. Nov23 isolated Windows #45053779999 late4-of16 nochange Alloc=8049 Out=0; registry Alloc=619727, Out=16061, Xperf OutKB=890.8; zero loss and precleanup interval, but top1024 full-stack parser rejected. Follow-up Windows #45058803441 separately reproduces nochange 8050/0 and registry 619729/16061 OutKB=890.8, proving numerical repeatability in the SAME 4-of-16 scoped type of run, NOT a leaked GIO object. Of 1024 Xperf stack rows, 31 violated Out#<=Alloc#; strict parser accepted 993 rows representing 15595 outstanding blocks, leaving 466 registry outstanding outside validated stack rows. The 1024-row limit was reached; missing 466 may be invalid rows and/or omitted top-k rows. No causal owner or global APC idle proven.
cases.why_previous_did_not_resolve: HeapWalk BUSY and REGION are different from PSAPI PrivateUsage; former only reports current blocks/selected regions. Prior ETW saved truncated top25 module frame occurrences, not matched allocation+free bytes or a complete call-site owner. Unproven worker quiescence biases endpoints. The corrected #45040046000 probe closes pre-workload event-start, circular overwrite, and missing local-symbol setup ONLY on a synthetic fixture. The filtered report has not yet been independently parsed into exact 16 outstanding / 5760 requested bytes and matching source stack, nor adapted to real GIO workload and global worker quiet boundary. Follow-up diagnosed that this WPT version's combined `-stacks -size 360 361` yielded no stack frames although unfiltered `-stacks -top 100` contained the synthetic symbol. `-totals -size ... -requireframes` did not isolate source count (e.g., 84 vs known64). Local parser now verifies unfiltered unique-source stack 64/16, so that synthetic gap is FIXED. No proof yet of true GIO owner across completed worker epochs. The watch subscription submechanism IS NOW bounded by both pinned source and runtime counts; previously only a source-level model had been available. It cannot explain the remaining owner-unknown GIO/WinRT and COM/heap commit residuals. Do not rerun watch bound as if unproven. Existing 256/512MB full-registry sequential ETW stopped HeapSession before safe stop, making owner inference impossible. New last4-of16 capture fixed logger exhaustion but revealed an Xperf source stack report shape/coverage difference. Previous parser did not preserve a safe error classification or independently extract aggregate Out# on failure; this is a diagnostic-instrument limitation, not a proven leak or an unexplained endpoint. Two genuine registry late-window captures are now available, unlike the earlier missing HeapSession. Full stack attribution still failed because 31 of 1024 Xperf rows reported Out#>Alloc# and top-1024 count was saturated; a further 466 outstanding blocks cannot be assigned to a validated stack. This is no longer generic 'unknown': specific Xperf row semantics and top-N truncation are the active diagnostic defects. The independent Xperf heap totals DO establish 16061 outstanding in both runs, not their expected lifetime. Avoid treating bad rows as OTHER or silently accepting out>alloc.
cases.missing_observable: Allocation IDs with matching frees and outstanding bytes grouped by sanitized module/source site on the same controlled lifetime boundary; commit movement by reserved/committed category, trace completeness and worker/APC idle provenance.
cases.next_automatic_action: Check newest Windows #45059395512 after commit 55aa7bd: its atomic controller/parser adds explicitly bounded well-formed source stack cohort counts and independent local Xperf -a heap -images aggregate fallback when top1024 stack parser fails. Compare total 16061 to safe image-group coverage, while treating invalid stack rows/unknown 466 as unclassified, and qualify any source as only top-frame membership. If image fallback fails, record structured reason and design one short exact per-source event-lifetime targeted test, not another blind 256/4h test. Confirm per-PID AppInfo worker/APC epoch and PrivateUsage/REGION before deciding LEAK_CONFIRMED/BOUNDED_RETENTION.
cases.decisive_rule: Two zero-loss registry late4 controls with Xperf heap `Out#=16061` (890.8 KiB rounded) establish *live at trace-stop* blocks, but NOT a leak, because active/lifetime boundaries are unknown. Nochange is 0 only for in-window allocations. Validated 15595 of 16061 stacks and 31 inconsistent top1024 rows are incomplete owner evidence. Only completed expected lifetimes + allocation/free ownership + comparable commit/PrivateUsage trend can close case. Registry status remains evidence_gap.

cases.scope: Original uninstrumented four-arm 256-cycle Combo Windows2022 CI (not same as three GIO16 runs)
cases.observed: Combo settled control-adjusted PSAPI PrivateUsage +368640B; late192-256 +53248B. HeapWalk 360-byte size bin late controlled +5 blocks, size is not allocation owner.
cases.why_previous_did_not_resolve: Original 256-cycle evidence saved aggregate endpoint counters, but no source-owned outstanding allocation lifetime or complete per-heap commit census. Instrumented 16-cycle and later UST traces are different processes/workloads; they cannot be backfilled as original allocation owners.
cases.missing_observable: Complete same-arm alloc/free ownership and committed/freeable region accounting at a proven quiet boundary for the specific late residual, preserving the original SDK and workload identity.
cases.next_automatic_action: First close GIO16_OWNER_AND_COMMIT's attribution and capture-completeness gate. Only then decide whether a differentiated short CI experiment can answer the original late residual; if not, predefine one minimal same-configuration window with a clear discriminating trace. Never rerun original four-arm 256 solely to repeat counters.
cases.decisive_rule: Classify only with same-workload lifetime evidence identifying an owned outstanding source or repeatable bounded retention; older 360B counts alone cannot settle either case.

cases.scope: CI-only Windows registry callbacks and GIO worker/APC parser cleanup
cases.observed: Archived phase trace reports worker_active_after_cleanup=1 and boundary_tick_ambiguous=1; 0-18 paired windows are not globally quiescent. Windows runtime #45046446784 shows APC delivery completed 17 times in registry 16-cycle arm, with 23 total re-registrations and 6 pending watches at the end. A pending watched key is normal: fully global APC queue idle NOT proven.
cases.why_previous_did_not_resolve: A finished AppInfo update counter does not acknowledge not-yet-delivered APCs or globally drain other async producers. Timed wait and GObject count alone can produce false leak/plateau conclusions. Even an observed per-key watch count bound is not a closed producer queue or worker quiescence acknowledgment. Watch counts quantify one source cohort only, and do not drain Windows APC or unrelated WinRT callbacks.
cases.missing_observable: Proven closed producer/consumer boundary, including callback arrivals, queued jobs, active worker count, update epoch completion and absence of delayed callback after snapshot.
cases.next_automatic_action: Use the CI-only pre-workload/pre-cleanup event fence to take reproducible before-cleanup allocation snapshots while recording APC watch transitions and existing AppInfo worker phase ordinals in the SAME run. Distinguish observed quiet/finished update epoch from unobservable future notifications; if no globally closed producer barrier exists, adopt scoped source-owned lifetime windows rather than inventing a global quiet state. AI CI only, no actual PC.
cases.decisive_rule: Counter zero is never sufficient. Any leak classification must name a verified allocation owner and expected lifetime, exclude active worker epochs, and transparently label outstanding notifications or future queue closure as unproven. Pending registry watches are bounded and expected at 6 in the specific Windows runner, not evidence of a leak.
